prerequisites: General requirements for access to the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of a company, types of companies, and the environment in which they operate.
Be able to understand the different subsystems that make up a company.
Understand the principles of business organization and management.
Knowledge of basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Mechanical Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Organization and management of companies.

syllabus_topics: Functioning of economic activity and types of markets
Topic 2: Company and typology of companies
Concept and objectives of the company
Types of companies: economic, organizational, and legal criteria
Asset and results analysis for decision-making
Valuation of investment and financing projects
teaching_methods: Case analysis from document reading and video viewing
Presentation of individual or group assignments
assessment_rules: The ordinary assessment includes a final theoretical-practical written exam (EX.ORD) worth a maximum of 6.5 points, requiring a minimum of 40% (2.6 points). Three assessable practices (P1, P2, P3) and participation (P) together are worth a maximum of 3.5 points (1 point for each practice, 0.5 for participation), requiring a minimum of 1.4 points (40%) from this block. The final grade is the sum of these components, but a minimum of 5 points overall is needed to pass. If the minimums for components are met but not the overall 5 points, the course is failed with the calculated score. If the overall score is above 5 points but a component minimum is not met, the final score is 4 points (fail). In extraordinary calls, students can take a theoretical-practical exam (EX.EXTR) and/or a practical exam (EX.PR), maintaining previously passed component scores.
